The launch-bound small/medium shapes (n=32 @14.5us, n=176 @265us, n=352 @618us) pay per-call host launch overhead across many tiny kernel launches. Collapse it with an EXPLICIT CUDA graph: build node-by-node (cudaGraphCreate/cudaGraphAddKernelNode), instantiate once and cache, re-launch each call updating data pointers via cudaGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams, launched on the NULL queue (literal 0 — NEVER type the banned substring 'stream'). Independent nodes get empty dependency lists so they can overlap. Guard against first-call pointer-capture staleness. Stretch: capture the entire per-call kernel sequence into one graph.

n=32 explicit CUDA graph (cudaGraphCreate/AddKernelNode/Instantiate built once, cached by B; cudaGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams updates data ptrs each call; cudaGraphLaunch(exec,0) on NULL queue). Profile confirms 1x Create/Add/Instantiate + 20100x Launch+SetParams. shape0 n=32 14.495->12.771us (-12%). geomean 1763.358->1742.081us.

Confirms launch-overhead premise pays only at n=32. Reverting.

FINAL: keep n=32 explicit CUDA graph, revert n=176 graph (GPU-bound). (2) n=352 (618us wall, 531us custom GPU, ~87us host gap across ~33 launches/call) CANNOT be graphed via the explicit-node API: its chain is panel(custom)->S,W(cuBLAS)->build_Minv(custom)->Y,C-=VY(cuBLAS) per block, so every custom kernel is isolated between cuBLAS nvjet bf16 GEMMs (~20/call) -- no contiguous custom run to capture, and cuBLAS can only be graphed via banned stream capture. n=352 B=40 (618us) has ~87us (14%) of host launch-gap across ~33 launches/call, but it is NOT graph-capturable: its per-outer-block chain interleaves custom kernels with ~20 cuBLAS bf16 nvjet GEMMs (panel->S,W cuBLAS->build_Minv->Y,C-=VY cuBLAS) and the explicit-node graph API cannot express cuBLAS calls (stream capture is banned). So attack it by KERNEL FUSION instead: fold the small per-block GEMMs (S=V^TC and build_Minv's tiny S=V^TV) into the custom panel/build_Minv kernels (custom WMMA on the bf16 trailing apply) so the cuBLAS launch breaks disappear, cutting the launch-gap directly AND making the remaining chain graph-capturable as a stretch. Brief-2 (n=176 megakernel COMPUTE opt). Best: n=176 264.8->261.8us (W=16 warps, committed 65e18a6f), a small REAL reproducible win (~1% shape, ~0.07% geomean). geomean ~1744us (parent 1742, within noise). Only fixable by splitting matrices across CTAs (infeasible: serial column dependency + resident smem) or a device-filling algorithm (the blocked path is slower for n=176). Small shapes (n32/n176/n352) are exhausted (you proved single-CTA-per-matrix is CTA-count-limited at B=40, not fixable). Redirect to n=4096 B=2 (11392us, the SINGLE LARGEST shape) -- vacated by W2, and it uses the CholeskyQR path (NOT the Householder panel W0/W2 are attacking, so fully orthogonal/no collision). W2 proved the FP64 cholesky is irreducible (cond(G)~1.6e9 needs FP64 stability) -- DO NOT touch the cholesky or Gram. Attack the OTHER ~60% of the 11.4ms: the TRSM (tri_solve_right_inv ~L5273) + the orhr_col recon (recon_lu_cpp ~L5542 + build_H_inplace). KEY enabler: the in-path tau-override makes householder_product orthonormal EXACTLY regardless of recon/TRSM precision, so ONLY the loose factor residual (rtol=20*4096*eps) binds. WARMUP micro (cheap, ncu-confirm first): the TRSM diagonal solve (~L5416-5429) is 3xTF32 (Rinvh@Xbh + Rinvh@Xbl + Rinvl@Xbh) -- try 1xTF32 (Rinvh@Xbh only); ~12% of TRSM FLOPs so expect low-single-%. BOLD macro: the recon's single-level blocked LU (recon_lu_cpp, ob=64) is itself partly serial -- restructure it (recursive/wider blocking, or fold build_H) so its GEMMs fill the device at B=2, OR find a cheaper direct path from (A,R) to V that avoids re-factoring Q entirely (only the factor residual binds). ncu the TRSM + recon GEMM occupancy at B=2 FIRST. BOUNDARY: you own n=4096; W0=n512/n2048, W2=n1024. Keep precision honest (factor gate must pass). Stacks on global best 1735.72.

TRSM warmup: 1xTF32 diagonal solve. REGRESSION shape6 11392->49833us (+338%), geomean 1735.72->1963.32. Validation PASSES (correct). Root cause: 1xTF32 Q too inaccurate -> _cholqr_path good-gate (colnorm_dev<=_COLNORM_TOL=5e-2) fails -> ALL B=2 fall back to torch.geqrf (~30ms FP64 QR each). The factor residual tolerates 1xTF32 but the tighter runtime orth proxy does not. Reverting.

Fold diag_lu into panel_solve_fused: REGRESSION shape6 11392->17104us (+50%), geomean ->1796.77. check pass (bit-correct). Root cause: the diagonal LU is a serial 64-step chain (64 syncs); folding it makes EVERY panel_solve CTA (33-66/matrix) redundantly pay the full serial chain in its prologue -> worse than the single grid=2 diag_lu it replaced (which did the serial work ONCE). Reverting.

FINAL brief-3: reverted both n=4096 attempts (TRSM 1xTF32 +338% via good-gate fallback; diag_lu fusion +50% via redundant serial chain) back to parent. geomean 1736.78 (parent 1735.72, within noise), shape6 n=4096 11380us == baseline. ncu B=2 root cause: recon diag_lu grid=2 0.06% SM ~2.1ms (barrier-latency, 64 syncs/panel, irreducible serial), panel_solve grid=33-66 6% warps ~2.7ms, both serial x64 panels; cholesky(39%)+Gram(12%) off-limits. The TRSM+recon are serial-latency-bound at B=2 (same CTA-count wall as small shapes, ~146 SMs idle); no precision/launch/fusion lever moves it without a device-filling non-serial recon algorithm.

Brief-3 (n=4096 B=2 TRSM+recon): thorough NEGATIVE, no win. Final geomean 1736.78us == parent global best 1735.72 (within noise; both attempts reverted, only a harmless set_trsm_diag1x knob at proven value 0 remains). ncu B=2 FIRST (sudo+fd shim; nsys can't trace the spawned child): full per-call breakdown = CHOL(fp64) 39% + GRAM(ozaki int8) 12% [BOTH off-limits, W2-proven FP64-irreducible] + RECON 25% + TRSM 19% [attackable]. RECON detail: diag_lu_warp grid=batch=2, 0.06% SM, ~33us x64 panels = ~2.1ms (BARRIER-LATENCY-bound: 64 syncs/panel serial chain, irreducible); panel_solve_fused grid=33-66, 6.24% warps active, ~2.7ms; both SERIAL across 64 panels. ATTEMPTS (both committed honestly then reverted): (1) WARMUP TRSM 3xTF32->1xTF32 diagonal: +338% REGRESSION (49833us). The 1xTF32 Q=A*Rinv is too inaccurate -> _cholqr_path's RUNTIME good-gate (colnorm_dev=|||Qcol||-1|<=_COLNORM_TOL=5e-2) fails -> ALL B=2 fall back to ~30ms FP64 torch.geqrf. CRITICAL CORRECTION to the brief's premise: the good-gate orth proxy, NOT the loose factor residual, is what binds the TRSM precision -- there is NO precision slack as long as that gate stands. (2) BOLD fold diag_lu into panel_solve: +50% REGRESSION (17104us, bit-correct). The serial 64-step diagonal LU then runs REDUNDANTLY in every one of the 33-66 panel_solve CTAs; the dedicated grid=2 diag_lu does the serial work ONCE. ROOT CAUSE (same as my n176/n352 finding): n=4096 B=2 leaves ~146 of 148 SMs idle, and the diagonal factorizations (TRSM diag pre-invert, recon diag_lu) have IRREDUCIBLE serial barrier chains -- a CTA-count + serial-chain wall. SUGGESTIONS: the only thing that moves this is a fundamentally DIFFERENT recon that is device-filling and non-serial -- e.g. a recursive/2-level blocked LU whose diagonal sub-factorizations are themselves blocked (shorter barrier depth), OR a blocked-WY orhr_col variant that is GEMM-heavy instead of substitution-heavy, OR relaxing/removing the _cholqr_path good-gate (would unlock the TRSM precision drop but is a secret-safety risk on held-out ill-cond shapes -- needs the manager's call). Lower-risk: the cholesky is 39% and 'irreducible' per W2 -- but if a mixed-precision (FP64 only on the ill-conditioned trailing) cholesky is ever revisited it dwarfs my targets. For now n=4096 is at its serial-latency floor.

n=4096 (11380us, single largest shape): you proved cholesky(39%)+gram(12%) are FP64-irreducible and TRSM-precision is locked by the good-gate. The UNATTACKED 25% is the orhr_col RECON (recon_lu_cpp): it's a single-level blocked LU that's SERIAL across 64 panels (diag_lu grid=2 at 0.06% SM, panel_solve grid=33-66 at 6% warps) -- barrier-latency-bound with ~146/148 SMs IDLE. Mechanism: make the recon DEVICE-FILLING and shorter-barrier-depth. Replace the single-level 64-panel substitution chain with a RECURSIVE / 2-level blocked LU whose diagonal sub-factorizations are themselves blocked (halves the barrier-chain depth per level), turning the substitution-heavy recon into GEMM-heavy work that fills idle SMs. This is the orhr_col reconstruction -- it must still produce V exact enough that build_H + the tau-override + factor residual hold (tau-override owns orthogonality; only the factor residual on the recon's V binds). SECONDARY if recon restructure stalls: the good-gate (colnorm_dev<=5e-2) forces 30ms geqrf fallback on TRSM imprecision -- since tau-override owns orthogonality, investigate whether the gate can be made to test what ACTUALLY binds (factor residual on the reconstructed H) rather than Q-column-norm, unlocking your TRSM precision drop -- but keep it SECRET-SAFE (the gate protects held-out ill-cond; gate on the real constraint, do not just loosen the threshold). ncu the recon GEMM fill. Must genuinely factor each input (guards forbid hacks). Stacks on global best 1723.58.

Brief-4 recon restructure: EARLY-EXIT as intractable (per brief clause), no code change. ncu re-confirms recon = panel_solve_fused (2.48ms, 3.5% SM, grid 8-126) + diag_lu_warp (1.93ms, 0.06% SM, grid=2) + Schur GEMMs (~1.7ms, 10-31% SM, already occupied), all SERIAL across 64 panels at B=2 (~146/148 SMs idle). KEY: the GEMM-ification the brief asks for was ALREADY TRIED and LOST -- the source (L5117) records 'at batch=2/n=4096 the cuBLAS trsm_right SIMT kernel underfills the 148 SMs', which is WHY the custom substitution panel_solve_fused replaced cuBLAS trsm. The recon's per-panel solve is fundamentally a THIN 64-wide op (no wide trailing to GEMM-fill within one panel, unlike the main TRSM which blocks a full n-wide solve). diag_lu is an irreducibly-serial 64-step LU (can't GEMM-ify -- it IS the factorization). 2-level blocking leaves diag_lu+panel_solve counts unchanged (they dominate), so no help. baseline geomean 1732.49, n=4096 11388us (unchanged).

Brief-4 (recon restructure + good-gate secondary): EARLY-EXIT, both paths intractable -- reported honestly per the brief's clause. No code change; geomean stays 1732.49 (parent global best). PRIMARY (recon 2-level/recursive blocked LU): ncu re-confirmed recon = panel_solve_fused (2.48ms, 3.5% SM) + diag_lu_warp (1.93ms, 0.06% SM, grid=2) + Schur GEMMs (~1.7ms, already 10-31% SM occupied), serial across 64 panels at B=2. DECISIVE finding: the GEMM-ification the brief proposes was ALREADY TRIED AND LOST -- source comment L5117 records 'at batch=2/n=4096 the cuBLAS trsm_right SIMT kernel underfills the 148 SMs', which is the documented REASON the custom substitution panel_solve_fused replaced cuBLAS trsm in the first place. The recon's per-panel solve is a THIN 64-wide op (no wide trailing to GEMM-fill within one panel; the main Q=A*Rinv TRSM already DOES use the blocked-wide-GEMM fill because it blocks a full n-wide solve). diag_lu is an irreducibly-serial 64-step LU (can't GEMM-ify; it IS the factorization). 2-level blocking leaves the diag_lu+panel_solve counts (the dominant 4.4ms) unchanged. SECONDARY (good-gate -> unlock TRSM 1xTF32): also net-negative. The colnorm_dev gate is O(n^2)-cheap; a SAFE factor-residual gate must compute householder_product(H,tau) + Q_hp^T*A = TWO n^3 GEMMs ~= 1.8ms at n=4096, which EXCEEDS the TRSM 1xTF32 saving (~0.5ms, ~12% of TRSM). There is no O(n^2) proxy for the factor residual (it needs Q_hp^T*A). So gating on the real constraint costs more than it unlocks; only loosening the threshold would be cheap, but that is the reward-hack the brief forbids. CONCLUSION: n=4096 B=2 is at its B=2 serial-latency optimum across cholesky(FP64-irreducible), gram(FP64-irreducible), TRSM(blocked-GEMM-fill already + gate-locked precision), and recon(custom-substitution already beat trsm; diag_lu irreducibly serial). The shape's floor is the ~146/148 idle SMs at B=2 -- only more batch or a fundamentally non-serial QR would move it, neither available. RECOMMENDATION: stop attacking n=4096 (3 briefs, all confirm the same wall); the geomean headroom is on the large-BATCH shapes (n512 B=640, n1024 B=60) where W0/W2 have GEMM-fill room.

n4096 fully walled (you confirmed, 3 briefs) -- redirect to the 25%-gap question. HYPOTHESIS for #1's edge: we carry DEFENSIVE higher-than-FP16 precision on WELL-CONDITIONED shapes that could be pure FP16. MEASURE it: for each well-conditioned benchmark shape (n512 cond2 dense, n1024 cond2, n2048 cond1, n32, n176, n352), does an END-TO-END FP16 panel factorization + tau-override (orthogonality free, ~300x margin per W0) + R:=triu(H) set from triu(Q_fp16^T A) PASS the factor gate? So the FP16 Q binds the residual against A; that residual (scaled, FP64-measured) IS your deliverable per shape. Report a PASS/FAIL + scaled-factor-residual + speedup-vs-current TABLE for the 6 well-cond shapes. Goal: find which well-cond shapes can drop to uniform FP16 (the likely gap source). Do NOT touch the ill-cond shapes (band/rowscale walled, W0/W2 own them); the 'mixed' shapes still need the per-matrix demote fallback so don't over-generalize a passing dense table to mixed. ncu/benchmark each. If a shape passes AND is faster, that's a bankable win -- implement+validate+commit it; if all well-cond shapes are already at FP16 (no defensive precision to drop), report that (it means the gap is elsewhere). Stacks on global best.
